Data Preparation - SILC

Joana Martins

2026-02-10

Initial Processing of the Dataset

First step was reading the provided subset of SILC data

library(readxl)
## Warning: package 'readxl' was built under R version 4.5.3
SILC <- read_xlsx("C:/Users/PC/Documents/Estágio e Dissertação/SILC2.xlsx")

Then, removed variables that won’t be used

library(dplyr)
## Warning: package 'dplyr' was built under R version 4.5.3
## 
## Attaching package: 'dplyr'
## The following objects are masked from 'package:stats':
## 
##     filter, lag
## The following objects are masked from 'package:base':
## 
##     intersect, setdiff, setequal, union
SILC <- SILC %>% select(-c(HB110, HH021, HH030, PB205, PB200, RB081
                           , DECILE, QUINTILE, PL032, PB190, PL051A))

For more intuitive understanding, renamed the variables

names(SILC)[names(SILC) == "RB030"] <- "PersonalID"
names(SILC)[names(SILC) == "RB040"] <- "HhID"
names(SILC)[names(SILC) == "RB050"] <- "PersonalWeight"
names(SILC)[names(SILC) == "DB090"] <- "HhWeight"
names(SILC)[names(SILC) == "RB082"] <- "Age"
names(SILC)[names(SILC) == "RB090"] <- "Gender"
names(SILC)[names(SILC) == "HB120"] <- "HhSize"
names(SILC)[names(SILC) == "RB280"] <- "CountryBirth"
names(SILC)[names(SILC) == "RB290"] <- "Citizenship"
names(SILC)[names(SILC) == "PE041"] <- "EducationalLevel"
names(SILC)[names(SILC) == "RB211"] <- "ActivityStatus"
names(SILC)[names(SILC) == "PB230"] <- "FatherCountryBirth"
names(SILC)[names(SILC) == "PB240"] <- "MotherCountryBirth"
names(SILC)[names(SILC) == "PL145"] <- "FullPartTime"
names(SILC)[names(SILC) == "HB130"] <- "InterviewMode"
names(SILC)[names(SILC) == "PL040A"] <- "EmploymentStatus"

names(SILC)
##  [1] "PersonalID"         "FullPartTime"       "InterviewMode"     
##  [4] "EmploymentStatus"   "HhID"               "PersonalWeight"    
##  [7] "Age"                "Gender"             "HhSize"            
## [10] "HhWeight"           "CountryBirth"       "Citizenship"       
## [13] "EducationalLevel"   "ActivityStatus"     "FatherCountryBirth"
## [16] "MotherCountryBirth"

Multiply weights to match the whole population since we are only using a subset of SILC

SILC <- SILC %>%
  mutate(PersonalWeight = PersonalWeight * (12871 / 5000))

Inspection and Recoding of Variables

To match the formatting of GEM data, a comparative analysis was carried out prior to the descriptive documentation of the variables in each of the surveys in order to consider the best way to perform the matching. Let’s look at each variable one by one.

Age

str(SILC$Age)
##  num [1:5000] 53 43 37 35 51 51 20 16 17 58 ...
SILC <- SILC %>%
  mutate(Age = case_when(
    Age < 18 ~ "0-17",
    Age >= 18 & Age <= 24 ~ "18-24",
    Age >= 25 & Age <= 34 ~ "25-34",
    Age >= 35 & Age <= 44 ~ "35-44",
    Age >= 45 & Age <= 54 ~ "45-54",
    Age >= 55 & Age <= 64 ~ "55-64",
    Age >= 65 ~ "65+",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  ))

SILC$Age <- factor(SILC$Age, 
                   levels = c("0-17","18-24","25-34","35-44","45-54","55-64","65+")
)


library(tibble)
## Warning: package 'tibble' was built under R version 4.5.3
age_distribution <- SILC %>%
  group_by(Age) %>%
  summarise(
    Count = n(),                                          
    Weighted_Count = sum(PersonalWeight, na.rm = TRUE)  
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Percentage = round(Count / sum(Count) * 100, 1),
    Weighted_Percentage = round(Weighted_Count / sum(Weighted_Count) * 100, 1)
  )

age_distribution <- age_distribution %>%
  mutate(Age = as.character(Age)) %>%
  bind_rows(tibble(
    Age = "Total",
    Count = sum(.$Count),
    Weighted_Count = sum(.$Weighted_Count),
    Percentage = 100,
    Weighted_Percentage = 100
  ))

print(age_distribution)

SILC <- SILC %>%

SILC$Age <- droplevels(SILC$Age)

age_distribution2 <- SILC %>%
  group_by(Age) %>%

age_distribution2 <- age_distribution2 %>%

    Age = "Total",

Country of birth

str(SILC$CountryBirth)
##  chr [1:3183] "FR" "CZ" "FR" "SK" "FR" "FR" "LU" "ES" "ES" "ES" "EL" "IT" ...
library(countrycode)
## Warning: package 'countrycode' was built under R version 4.5.3
SILC <- SILC %>%
  mutate(
    CountryBirth = case_when(
      CountryBirth == "EL" ~ "GR",
      CountryBirth == "UK" ~ "GB",
      TRUE ~ CountryBirth
    ),
    Continent = suppressWarnings(countrycode(CountryBirth, origin = "iso2c", destination = "continent")),
    CountryBirth = case_when(
      CountryBirth == "LU" ~ "Luxembourg",
      CountryBirth == "PT" ~ "Portugal",
      Continent == "Europe" | CountryBirth %in% c("XK", "GB") ~ "Other countries in Europe",
      (!is.na(Continent) & Continent != "Europe") | CountryBirth == "FOR" ~ "Rest of the World",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

SILC$CountryBirth <- factor(SILC$CountryBirth,
  levels = c("Luxembourg", "Portugal", "Other countries in Europe", "Rest of the World")
)

countryb_distribution <- SILC %>%
  group_by(CountryBirth) %>%
  summarise(
    Count = n(),                                          
    Weighted_Count = sum(PersonalWeight, na.rm = TRUE)  
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Percentage = round(Count / sum(Count) * 100, 1),
    Weighted_Percentage = round(Weighted_Count / sum(Weighted_Count) * 100, 1)
  )

countryb_distribution <- countryb_distribution %>%
  mutate(CountryBirth = as.character(CountryBirth)) %>%
  bind_rows(tibble(
    CountryBirth = "Total",
    Count = sum(.$Count),
    Weighted_Count = sum(.$Weighted_Count),
    Percentage = 100,
    Weighted_Percentage = 100
  ))

print(countryb_distribution)

Parent’s country of birth

SILC <- SILC %>%
  mutate(
    ParentsCountryBirth = case_when(
      FatherCountryBirth == "LU" & MotherCountryBirth == "LU" ~ "Luxembourg",
      FatherCountryBirth == "LU" & is.na(MotherCountryBirth) ~ NA_character_,
      is.na(FatherCountryBirth) & MotherCountryBirth == "LU" ~ NA_character_,
      is.na(FatherCountryBirth) & is.na(MotherCountryBirth) ~ NA_character_,
      TRUE ~ "Abroad"
    )

Employment Status

str(SILC$EmploymentStatus)
##  num [1:3183] 3 3 3 2 3 NA NA 3 2 3 ...
SILC %>%
  count(EmploymentStatus)
## # A tibble: 5 × 2
##   EmploymentStatus     n
##              <dbl> <int>
## 1                1    97
## 2                2   101
## 3                3  1979
## 4                4     2
## 5               NA  1004
SILC <- SILC %>%
  mutate(
    EmploymentStatus = case_when(
      EmploymentStatus == 1 ~ "Self-employed",
      EmploymentStatus == 2 ~ "Self-employed",
      EmploymentStatus == 3 ~ "Employee",
      EmploymentStatus == 4 ~ "Employee",
      is.na(EmploymentStatus) & ActivityStatus != "Employed" ~ "Unemployed+Inactive",
      is.na(EmploymentStatus) & ActivityStatus == "Employed" ~ NA_character_,
      is.na(EmploymentStatus) & is.na(ActivityStatus) ~ NA_character_,
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    EmploymentStatus = factor(EmploymentStatus, 
                              levels = c("Self-employed", 
                                         "Employee", 
                                         "Unemployed+Inactive"))
  )

emp_distribution <- SILC %>%
  group_by(EmploymentStatus) %>%
  summarise(
    Count = n(),                                          
    Weighted_Count = sum(PersonalWeight, na.rm = TRUE)  
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Percentage = round(Count / sum(Count) * 100, 1),
    Weighted_Percentage = round(Weighted_Count / sum(Weighted_Count) * 100, 1)
  )

emp_distribution <- emp_distribution %>%
  mutate(EmploymentStatus = as.character(EmploymentStatus)) %>%
  bind_rows(tibble(
    EmploymentStatus = "Total",
    Count = sum(.$Count),
    Weighted_Count = sum(.$Weighted_Count),
    Percentage = 100,
    Weighted_Percentage = 100
  ))

print(emp_distribution)
## # A tibble: 4 × 5
##   EmploymentStatus    Count Weighted_Count Percentage Weighted_Percentage
##   <chr>               <int>          <dbl>      <dbl>               <dbl>
## 1 Self-employed         198         29913.        6.2                 6.9
## 2 Employee             1981        269221.       62.2                62.2
## 3 Unemployed+Inactive  1004        133519.       31.5                30.9
## 4 Total                3183        432653.      100                 100
library(tidyr)
## Warning: package 'tidyr' was built under R version 4.5.3
SILC %>%
  count(EmploymentStatus, ActivityStatus, wt = PersonalWeight, name = "weighted_n") %>%
  group_by(ActivityStatus) %>%
  mutate(percent = round(100 * weighted_n / sum(weighted_n), 2)) %>%
  ungroup() %>% 
  select(EmploymentStatus, ActivityStatus, percent) %>% 
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = ActivityStatus,
    values_from = percent,
    values_fill = 0
  )

Full or Part-time Job

str(SILC$FullPartTime)
##  num [1:3183] 1 NA 1 1 1 NA NA 1 2 1 ...
SILC %>%
  count(FullPartTime)
## # A tibble: 3 × 2
##   FullPartTime     n
##          <dbl> <int>
## 1            1  1757
## 2            2   375
## 3           NA  1051
SILC <- SILC %>%
  mutate(
    FullPartTime = case_when(
      FullPartTime == 1 ~ "Full-time",
      FullPartTime == 2 ~ "Part-time",
      is.na(FullPartTime) & ActivityStatus != "Employed" ~ "Unemployed+Inactive",
      is.na(FullPartTime) & ActivityStatus == "Employed" ~ NA_character_,
      is.na(FullPartTime) & is.na(ActivityStatus) ~ NA_character_,
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
  )


SILC$FullPartTime = factor(SILC$FullPartTime, 
                                levels = c("Full-time", "Part-time", "Unemployed+Inactive"))

                           
full_distribution <- SILC %>%
  group_by(FullPartTime) %>%
  summarise(
    Count = n(),                                          
    Weighted_Count = sum(PersonalWeight, na.rm = TRUE)  
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Percentage = round(Count / sum(Count) * 100, 1),
    Weighted_Percentage = round(Weighted_Count / sum(Weighted_Count) * 100, 1)
  )

full_distribution <- full_distribution %>%
  mutate(FullPartTime = as.character(FullPartTime)) %>%
  bind_rows(tibble(
    FullPartTime = "Total",
    Count = sum(.$Count),
    Weighted_Count = sum(.$Weighted_Count),
    Percentage = 100,
    Weighted_Percentage = 100
  ))

print(full_distribution)

The result obtained (p < 0.001) allowed us to reject the hypothesis that the data are missing completely at random (MCAR).

Missing indicator variables were created for each of the incomplete variables, and logistic regression models were estimated, using all fully observed variables.

library(brglm2)
## Warning: package 'brglm2' was built under R version 4.5.3
vars_with_missing <- c("ParentsCountryBirth",
                       "EducationalLevel",
                       "Citizenship",
                       "FullPartTime")

for(v in vars_with_missing){
  SILC[[paste0("miss_", v)]] <- as.numeric(is.na(SILC[[v]]))
}


predictors <- c("Age", "Gender", "CountryBirth",
                "EmploymentStatus", "ActivityStatus",
                "HhSize")


models <- list()

for(v in vars_with_missing){
  formula <- as.formula(
    paste0("miss_", v, " ~ ", paste(predictors, collapse = " + "))
  )
  
  models[[v]] <- glm(formula, 
                     data = SILC, 
                     family = binomial,
                     method = "brglmFit")
  
  cat("\n\n----------------------------------\n")
  cat(" Missingness model for:", v, "\n")
  cat("----------------------------------\n")
  print(summary(models[[v]]))
}

Imputation using MICE

For the imputation model, - m = 30 is a conservative and stable choice when several variables have moderate missingness; it increases the accuracy of quantities derived from imputations (lower Monte Carlo variance) compared to minimum values (e.g., m=5). - maxit = 15 is sufficient for convergence in the chains (verified via trace/strip plots). seed ensures reproducibility.

ini  <- mice(data_to_imp, maxit = 0, printFlag = FALSE)
meth <- ini$method
pred <- ini$predictorMatrix

meth[] <- ""
meth["EducationalLevel"]    <- "polr"     
meth["ParentsCountryBirth"]  <- "logreg"   
meth["Citizenship"]         <- "polyreg"  
meth["FullPartTime"]        <- "polyreg"  

diag(pred) <- 0

visit <- c("Citizenship", "ParentsCountryBirth",
           "FullPartTime", "EducationalLevel")

imp_model <- mice(
  data_to_imp,
  m = 30,                 
  maxit = 15,           
  method = meth,
  predictorMatrix = pred,
  visitSequence = visit,
  seed = 20260212,
  printFlag = FALSE
)
## Warning: Number of logged events: 1800

Evaluation of results of imputation

plot(imp_model) 

stripplot(imp_model, Citizenship)

stripplot(imp_model, ParentsCountryBirth)

stripplot(imp_model, FullPartTime)

stripplot(imp_model, EducationalLevel)

set.seed(42)
completed_data <- complete(imp_model, sample(1:imp_model$m, 1))
compare_tables <- function(original, imputed, varname) {
  cat("\n==============================\n")
  cat(varname, "\n")
  cat("Original:\n")
  print(table(original, useNA = "always"))
  cat("\nImputed:\n")
  print(table(imputed, useNA = "always"))
  cat("==============================\n\n")
}

compare_tables(SILC$EducationalLevel, completed_data$EducationalLevel, "EducationalLevel")

library(ggplot2)
## Warning: package 'ggplot2' was built under R version 4.5.3
plot_compare <- function(original, imputed, varname, drop_na = TRUE, top_n = NULL) {
  df <- bind_rows(
    data.frame(Category = as.character(original), Type = "Original"),
    data.frame(Category = as.character(imputed),  Type = "Imputed")
  )

  if (drop_na) {
    df <- df |> filter(!is.na(Category))
  }

  df <- df |>
    mutate(Category = forcats::fct_infreq(Category))

  ggplot(df, aes(x = Category, fill = Type)) +
    geom_bar(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
    labs(
      title = paste("Distribution -", varname, "(Original vs Imputed)"),
      x = varname,
      y = "Frequency"
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("Original" = "#7FB3D5", "Imputed" = "#82E0AA")) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
      legend.position = "top",
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
    )
}

plot_compare(SILC$EducationalLevel,   completed_data$EducationalLevel,   "EducationalLevel", top_n = 10)

plot_compare(SILC$ParentsCountryBirth, completed_data$ParentsCountryBirth, "ParentsCountryBirth", top_n = 10)

plot_compare(SILC$FullPartTime,       completed_data$FullPartTime,       "FullPartTime", top_n = 10)
